Refit a banded-ridge model on all rows and return its weight matrix

Source: R/banded_ridge_weights.R
banded_ridge_weights.Rd

Cross-validated accuracies come from [run_banded_ridge()]; this function answers a different question: *what* each response is tuned to. Every response is refit once on all observations, using the hyperparameters it selected most often across the outer folds, and the coefficients are returned as one features-by-responses matrix. That matrix is the input for contrasts over feature columns and for principal-component summaries of tuning.

Usage

banded_ridge_weights(
  model,
  result,
  standardized = TRUE,
  target_batch_size = model$target_batch_size
)

Arguments

model

A `banded_ridge_model`.

result

The result of `run_banded_ridge(model)`.

standardized

If `TRUE` (default), coefficients are per standard deviation of each feature, which makes columns with different units comparable. If `FALSE`, coefficients are in the units of the feature matrix.

target_batch_size

Number of responses read and fit at once.

Value

A list of class `banded_ridge_weights` with

weights

Numeric matrix, features in rows and responses in columns.

set

Feature-band label of each row.

voxel_index

Mask index of each column.

hyperparameters

One row per response: the selected candidate, its `alpha` and band weights, and in how many outer folds it was chosen.

standardized

The `standardized` argument.

contrast_weights

Contrasts-by-responses matrix: the weights projected onto the contrasts declared in `feature_sets(contrasts = )`, or `NULL` when none were declared.

If the model has nuisance regressors they are regressed out of features and responses (with an intercept) before the refit.

Details

The weights are descriptive. They are estimated from all rows, so they must not be used to score predictions on those rows.

See also

[banded_ridge_model()], [run_banded_ridge()]
